text: Protein content of common raw materials for pig feed: fish meal 40–65%, soybean 40%, wheat bran 12–14%, rice bran 9–12%, corn 9%, rice 6%, cassava only 2%. If amino acids are insufficient, simply adding more protein or energy will not fix growth — 4 amino acids are essential for growth: lysine (the most important, often needs adding), methionine (usually adequate in raw materials), threonine (second most limiting after lysine, often needs adding), and tryptophan (rice usually supplies enough). Energy comes from fat (soybean and rice bran, being oil-rich, provide a lot of energy) and starch (rice, cassava, corn). Vitamins and minerals are never sufficient from raw materials alone for fast-growing pigs — a commercial premix supplying vitamins A, D, E, B and minerals (iron, zinc, magnesium, etc.) is needed and must be mixed into the diet daily to ensure good growth, reproduction, and health.
